lab.fallback: The 3D model cannot be shown on this device. The phases of the stroke are described below.
lab.drag: Drag the image to turn the camera.
lab.modelNote: Biomechanical model: positions solved with inverse kinematics along the real phases of the stroke.

phases.title: Ready position
phases.text: Weight on the balls of the feet, knees slightly bent, racquet in front of the body. The split step is timed with the opponent's strike.

phases.title: Shoulder turn
phases.text: The trunk rotates about its long axis until the shoulders pass 90° to the net. The free arm stays extended towards the ball, for balance and anticipation.

phases.title: Loop and racquet drop
phases.text: The racquet traces a loop and drops below the ball. Bending the knees loads the extensor muscles and prepares the low-to-high drive.

phases.title: Contact
phases.text: Contact in front of the right hip, with the racquet face perpendicular to the ground. Energy flows through the kinetic chain: legs, hips, trunk, shoulder, elbow, wrist.

phases.title: Follow-through and finish
phases.text: The forearm pronates (the “windscreen wiper”), the racquet rises over the left shoulder and the body recovers its balance for the next shot.

phases.title: Ready position
phases.text: Backhand grip prepared, with the left hand on the handle above the right. Split step as the opponent strikes.

phases.title: Shoulder turn
phases.text: The shoulders turn left past 90° and both hands take the racquet back beside the left hip; the weight moves onto the back leg.

phases.title: Racquet drop
phases.text: The racquet head drops below the ball's path for a low-to-high stroke, knees bent and trunk stable.

phases.title: Contact
phases.text: Contact in front of the left hip, arms almost straight. The left hand drives the stroke while the right hand steadies the racquet.

phases.title: Finish
phases.text: The racquet finishes over the right shoulder. A full trunk rotation and the weight transfer onto the front leg control the depth of the ball.

phases.title: Starting position
phases.text: Feet in the platform stance, shoulders perpendicular to the net, ball and racquet together in front of the body.

phases.title: Ball toss
phases.text: The straight left arm rises and releases the ball above the right shoulder, slightly in front of the body, without spin.

phases.title: Trophy position
phases.text: Knees bent, shoulders tilted with the left one high, right elbow at shoulder height: elastic energy builds before the drive.

phases.title: Back loop and extension
phases.text: The racquet drops behind the shoulders, then the explosive leg drive and trunk rotation accelerate the kinetic chain from the ground up.

phases.title: Contact
phases.text: Contact at the highest point with the arm fully extended. Forearm pronation and wrist flexion give the ball its speed and spin.

phases.title: Landing and finish
phases.text: Landing on the left foot inside the court, with the racquet carrying on to the left side of the body; balance allows a reaction to the return.
